focus: correctness — the validator's goal measurement against the runtime extractor

findingDetails.title: Runtime extractor and validator measure different durable slices once a fence carries trailing whitespace
findingDetails.evidence:
The runtime fence tolerates trailing spaces or tabs (`goal-slice.cjs:24`: `---[ 	]*
([\s\S]*?)
---[ 	]*(?:
|$)`) while the validator's goal copy does not (`spec-doc-structure.ts:1028`), so a tolerant document falls through to `body = normalized` and the frontmatter is measured as part of the durable slice. Observed with both production modules on one fixture: runtime 3903 characters (warn tier), validator 4008 characters (over tier, SPECDOC_SUFFICIENCY_005 error), delta exactly the 105-character frontmatter, and the validator slice contains the fixture's `SECRET-SESSION`. Exact fences agree exactly. The vitest fixture writes only `'---'` fences (spec-doc-structure.vitest.ts:209-233) and no test compares the two slices; ADR-003's promised golden pin against `continuity-freshness.ts:17` — which tolerates `\s*` — does not exist.
findingDetails.impact: `validate.sh --strict` can fail a packet whose runtime measurement sits in the warning band, quoting a length that includes bookkeeping the manifest excludes (`spec-kit-docs.json:25`). Fail-closed, so no exposure.
findingDetails.recommendation: Mirror the tolerant fence into the goal rule or import one shared matcher, and add the cross-surface parity test ADR-003 promises with a tolerant-fence fixture. Report only; no fix in this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both production modules loaded and executed on the same fixture; three regexes, the manifest measure and the vitest fixture read directly.

results.summary: ADR-003 promises one extractor pinned by a golden test against the validator's regex; the runtime and the validator now disagree on a tolerant fence and no pinning test exists.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: Cross-runtime goal contract with a shared slice module, a parallel plugin implementation, a validator measurement boundary and a packet that claims the fix.
